descriptionChirho: Intransitive physical posture of standing or stationing oneself, including taking a stand or remaining upright (Nifal stem across all inflections).
Lexicalized Nifal participle used as a substantive noun meaning an appointed official, overseer, or governor (Arabic وَكِيل / مُوَكَّل 'deputy, agent').
Abstract Nifal sense of being firmly established or enduring, distinguished by Arabic ثَابِتَة 'firm, stable' rather than وَاقِف 'standing'.
Causative action of setting up, erecting, or stationing someone or something in place (Arabic نَصَبَ / أَقَامَ 'to erect, set up').
Abstract causative sense of establishing or confirming something authoritatively, distinguished by Arabic يُثَبِّتُ 'to make firm' from the concrete 'set up' sense.

labelChirho: Hofal: be set up, be decreed
descriptionChirho: Passive of the causative stem indicating something has been erected, set in place, or authoritatively decreed (Arabic مَنْصُوبَة 'erected' and أُقِيمَت 'was established').
